title: Solution to the DOM Challenge
summary: Article giving the one-line console solution to the previous challenge: reach body from document, find the ul, take its last child and set its innerHTML.

concepts.heading: How the solution works
points: .lastElementChild on html is body (head is the first child).
.querySelector("ul") searches inside body only, returning the first ul. querySelector can be called on any element, not just document, and searches that element's descendants.
.lastElementChild of the ul is the third li (child elements only, text nodes ignored).
Assigning to .innerHTML replaces the li's content with the new text.
Why querySelector instead of another lastElementChild: the last child of body is the script element, so a pure child chain needs the ul to be picked out by selector or by index (children[3]).
